newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent clings falls on Iraqi oil export news.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent clings falls on Iraqi oil export news.

text.p: IPE Brent futures fell on Tuesday on news that Iraq expected to start exporting oil from the second six month tranche of its oil-for-food deal with the United Nations, traders said.
August IPE Brent was trading 16 cents lower at $17.82 a barrel at 1652 GMT, while July gas oil was 25 cents down at $161.00 a tonne.
Traders attibuted the drop to news that Iraqi oil minister Amir Rasheed told reporters in Madrid he expected Iraq to resume exporting oil under the oil-for-food deal in the next week to ten days.
Prior to the news the market had been fairly quiet as traders took a cautious approach ahead of the OPEC meeting in Vienna.
Few were expecting anything radical out of the meeting.
"People are playing it safe waiting to see what OPEC does even though they're not expecting much," said one trader.
Many players were expecting OPEC to rollover its current 25.03 million barrels per day output ceiling.
Comments on Tuesday by Saudi Arabian oil minister Ali bin Ibrahim al-Naimi bolstered this view. "A rollover is good if everyone adheres to their quota," he said.
